title: Annotatio II NATIVITAS: Rupert’s Exodus — bread/wine substance joined, not destroyed, into body-unity
pass_a_gloss: Then in the Commentary on Exodus bk. 2 ch. 10 with a fuller exposition: Just as, he says, He did not destroy human nature when by His operation from the virgin’s womb GOD by the Word joined it into unity of person; So He does not change or destroy the SUBSTANCE of bread and wine, according to the exterior species subject to the five senses, when He JOINS these to the same Word into the UNITY of the same body which hung on the cross, and of the same blood which He poured from His side. In the same place: Therefore just as we rightly and Catholicly confess as God the man who, taken from the virgin, hung on the cross, so truly we call Christ this which we take from the holy altar, we preach the Lamb of God.
pass_b_english: Exodus commentary (II.10): as God did not destroy human nature when joining it into personal unity from the virgin’s womb, so He does not destroy bread-and-wine substance when joining it to the Word into unity of the crucified body and shed blood.
What we take from the altar we truly call Christ, the Lamb of God — as we confess the virgin-born man on the cross to be God.
source_text: Tum Commentario in Exodum, Lib. 2. cap. 10. expositione auctiori: Sicut, inquit, humanam naturam non destruxit, cùm illam operatione sua ex utero virginis DEUS verbo in unitatem personae conjunxit; Sic SUBSTANTIAM panis & vini, secundum exteriorem speciem, quinque sensibus subactam, non mutat aut destruit, cum eidem Verbo, in UNITATEM corporis ejusdem, quod in cruce pependit, & sanguinis ejusdem quem de latere suo fudit, ista CONJUNGIT. Ibidem: Proinde sicut hominem, ait, qui de virgine sumtus in cruce pependit, rectè & Catholicè Deum confitemur, sic veraciter hoc, quod sumimus de sancto altari, Christum dicimus, agnum Dei praedicamus.
